command: pre-registration: S2RGS, scene 2 (LIVING_ROOM_SCENE5) on NEW states, layout O: SR 68's ReGuide port with perception everywhere (rgp), simulator poses everywhere (rgo), the held-mug pose from the simulator (rgoH) and the target-plate pose from the simulator (rgoT), against I, on frozen pi0.5 (docs/SCAFFOLD_RESULTS.md 72)

metrics.arms:
everything not named here is s2rg.py's client, line for line: entities, round declaration, statistics
results/flawed/s2rg/rg_stats_s2.json, registration at the first gated step, re-detection at ProprioHeld onsets, Hp's held-mug identity rule
(nearest perceived mug within HELD_R = .08 m of the hand), the interaction state "the instructed mug is held", the hand-back handling; prompt
and images never changed):
  - rgp   perception everywhere (SR 68's arm): OWLv2 sidecar + rendered depth + camera calibration (s2fix3.Percept, constants unchanged).
          While attached, the instructed mug follows the hand rigidly from the offset fixed at the attachment.
  - rgo   simulator everywhere (SR 68's privileged arm): simulator body positions of every mug and plate at every step; rg.py's oracle
          interaction rule on the instructed mug.
  - rgoH  rgp, but the HELD-mug pose comes from the simulator: from the attachment step (perceived: ProprioHeld onset + the perceived
          identity rule, as rgp) until the release, the instructed mug's position is the simulator body position; at the release the
          mug's remembered position is the simulator position (rgp: where the hand left it by the rigid estimate).  The target plate,
          the other plate, the resting mugs (including the instructed mug before the attachment) and the hold events are perceived.
  - rgoT  rgp, but the TARGET-plate pose comes from the simulator (the instructed destination's body position, set at the registration);
          the held mug (rigid estimate), the other plate, all mugs and the hold events are perceived.  The target plate is then always
          "perceived", so ReGuide is active in episodes where rgp could not find the plate (the pose source includes existence).
  - The rigid perceived held-mug estimate is also LOGGED at each release of rgoH (never fed), and every arm logs the simulator's mug
    position, as SR 69's mechanism rows.

design.bootstrap: paired over states, B = 2000, numpy default_rng(0)

metrics.prediction:
S2RGS predictions (SR 72), written 2026-11-16 BEFORE any job of this probe (states, smoke or main), and before experiments/s2rgs.py was
run.  Nothing of this probe has been run.

What is tested.  In scene 2 (LIBERO-10 LIVING_ROOM_SCENE5) ReGuide with perception (rgp) reaches N1 .417 on frozen pi0.5 (SR 69),
with simulator poses (rgo) .833 (SR 68).  SR 69 found the rigid held-mug estimate 5.65 cm off at the N1 release (the real mug in the
release region on .20 of N1 releases), and a box tracker did not reduce that error, so "the N1 residual is the perceived held-mug carry"
is only consistent with the data.  This probe swaps ONE pose source at a time and leaves everything else as in rgp.  Arms (pi0.5 only,
frozen; 60 new states, seeds 1000000 + k, layout O, tasks K1 K2 N1 N2):
  I     the frozen policy alone.
  rgp   perception everywhere (SR 68's arm; replication).
  rgo   simulator poses everywhere, including the interaction rule (SR 68's privileged arm; replication).
  rgoH  rgp, but the HELD mug's pose comes from the simulator from the attachment to the release (the attachment itself, the hold
        identity, the resting mugs and both plates stay perceived).
  rgoT  rgp, but the TARGET plate's pose comes from the simulator (the held mug, the other plate, all mugs stay perceived).

Registered contrasts on N1 and on N1+N2 (paired bootstrap over states, B = 2000, seed 0): V1 rgoH - rgp; V2 rgoT - rgp; V3 rgo - rgoH.
Direction pre-registered: if the held-mug account is right, V1 > 0 (HELD POSE CARRIES) and V3 ~ 0.  The alternative accounts that
would break this: (A) the gap sits in the hold / interaction rule (rgo uses the simulator's co-motion rule, rgoH keeps the perceived
ProprioHeld onset and identity), which would leave V1 small and V3 > 0; (B) the gap sits in the target plate (V2 > 0); (C) the
policy's own behaviour after the hand-back dominates, so no single swap moves N1 (V1, V2 ~ 0, V3 > 0).

What I expect mechanistically.  SR 69's release error under rgp (5.65 cm median, p90 21.7) is large enough to explain a lost N1
release: the release region is smaller than that error.  With the simulator's mug position steering the carry, the controller no
longer works from a biased estimate, so N1 should move most of the way to rgo.  rgo also differs from rgoH in three ways that I
cannot separate before running: the hold event (oracle rise-and-co-motion rule against ProprioHeld), the registration of the
resting mugs and plates (perceived vs simulator, errors about .4 cm), and ReGuide being active in episodes where perception fails
to find the instructed mug or plate (rgp: one state per task in SR 69).  I expect those to leave a modest remainder.  The target
plate is perceived to about .4 cm (SR 68's rendered-depth registration), small against the release region, so rgoT should
change little.

Point predictions, pi0.5 (60 states per task):
  I     K1 ~1.00  K2 ~.98  N1 ~.00  N2 ~.00.
  rgp   K1+K2 ~.99, N1 ~.42, N2 ~.97, N1+N2 ~.70 (replicates SR 69 within +-.10 on N1: 80%).
  rgo   K1+K2 ~.99, N1 ~.83, N2 ~.98, N1+N2 ~.90 (replicates SR 68 within +-.10 on N1: 70%).
  rgoH  K1+K2 ~.99, N1 ~.70, N2 ~.97, N1+N2 ~.84.
  rgoT  K1+K2 ~.99, N1 ~.45, N2 ~.97, N1+N2 ~.71.
Registered contrasts, pi0.5 (n = 60 states, so a CI on N1 is about +-.14 around the point):
  V1 rgoH - rgp on N1: point +.28.  HELD POSE CARRIES (lo > 0): 80%; NO CLEAR DIFFERENCE: 19%; HELD POSE LOWERS: 1%.
     On N1+N2: point +.14; CARRIES 70%.
  V2 rgoT - rgp on N1: point +.03.  NO CLEAR DIFFERENCE: 80%; TARGET POSE CARRIES: 19%; LOWERS: 1%.  On N1+N2: NO CLEAR
     DIFFERENCE 80%.
  V3 rgo - rgoH on N1: point +.13.  NO CLEAR DIFFERENCE: 55%; REMAINDER IN OTHER POSES (lo > 0): 43%; rgo BELOW rgoH: 2%.
     EQUIVALENT (CI inside +-.10) on N1: 5% (the CI is too wide); on N1+N2: 10%.
  Held-mug account read as registered ("V1 > 0 and V3 ~ 0"): both hold jointly (V1 CARRIES and V3 NO CLEAR DIFFERENCE): 45%.
     V1 CARRIES with V3 REMAINDER: 35%.  V1 NO CLEAR DIFFERENCE: 19%.
  K1+K2 non-inferiority at -.05 against I (NON-INFERIOR: lo > -.05): rgp 90%, rgo 90%, rgoH 90%, rgoT 90% (each arm's K1+K2 point
     ~.99, so the interval is limited by I's K-room).
  rgoH FIX WORKS and MEETS BAR: 85% each.  rgoT FIX WORKS 90%, MEETS BAR 85%.
  I's K1+K2 >= .70 (TESTABLE): 99%.
Mechanism, pi0.5 (N1, descriptive):
  The white mug ends on no plate: rgp ~.52 (SR 69: .550), rgoH ~.25, rgoT ~.50, rgo ~.10.
  The rigid perceived estimate at the N1 release (logged in rgp and, never fed, in rgoH): median xy error ~5.5 cm (within 3.5-8.0
     cm: 70%); in rgoH the arm's own estimate is the simulator's (0 by construction).  The share of N1 releases whose rigid estimate
     lies in the release region while the mug does not: ~.15 or more (rgp SR 69: 3 of 44 = .07; 60%).
  Registration, rgp / rgoH: target plate median ~.42 cm, instructed mug ~.39 cm, side right ~1.0; one state per task may leave the
     mug or plate unperceived (ReGuide inactive); under rgoT the target plate is never missing.
C1 (reference planner on the new states): UNMET (N1-N2 < .80): 65% (SR 69 .783).
